document_check.note: The document is Vermeulen RJ, Andersson V, Banken J, Hannink G, Govers TM, Rovers MM, Olde Rikkert MGM. 'Limited generalizability and high risk of bias in multivariable models predicting conversion risk from mild cognitive impairment to dementia: A systematic review', Alzheimer's & Dementia 2025;21(4):e70069, doi:10.1002/alz.70069 (PROSPERO CRD42022275181). It includes 62 studies (41 machine-learning models, 11 regression models, 5 disease state indexes) appraised with PROBAST. This matches the cited sentence.

cited_result: The review's appraisal result: every one of the 62 included MCI-to-dementia conversion models was rated at high risk of bias with PROBAST (analysis domain high in all), most lacked external validation, and the authors conclude that no highly valid prediction model is available.
tool_reason: The cited result is a synthesis finding (the risk-of-bias profile and the conclusion drawn from it) from a registered systematic review with a two-database search, duplicate screening and PROBAST appraisal, so ROBIS judges whether the review's own methods could bias that finding.

domains.rationale: The protocol was registered in PROSPERO before the search was completed, and the eligibility criteria (multi-source multivariable models predicting conversion from MCI to dementia over at least two years, with internal validation) are explicit and fit the review question. The English-only restriction is the one limitation, and the authors state it.

signalling.question: 1.1 Did the review adhere to pre-defined objectives and eligibility criteria?
signalling.quote: The details of this systematic review have been registered in PROSPERO under registration number CRD42022275181.

signalling.question: 1.2 Were the eligibility criteria appropriate for the review question?
signalling.quote: multivariable prediction models for conversion from mild cognitive impairment (MCI) to dementia

signalling.question: 1.3 Were eligibility criteria unambiguous?
signalling.quote: Multi-source prediction models with >=2-year horizon and internal validation (as summarised from Section 2.2 Eligibility criteria).

signalling.question: 1.4 Were all restrictions in eligibility criteria based on study characteristics appropriate?
signalling.quote: We searched for studies that were published from inception to January 18 2024.

signalling.question: 1.5 Were any restrictions in eligibility criteria based on sources of information appropriate?
signalling.quote: Only articles published in the English language were considered for review.

domains.rationale: Two databases (PubMed and Embase) were searched from inception to 18 January 2024 and supplemented with backward and forward citation chasing of every eligible study. Title and abstract screening was done independently by two researchers with a third resolving disagreements. Full-text screening is described only as made 'by the authors', and five of 305 eligible full texts could not be retrieved; neither is likely to change the risk-of-bias profile of the included set.

signalling.question: 2.1 Did the search include an appropriate range of databases/electronic sources for published and unpublished reports?
signalling.quote: We systematically searched the databases PubMed and Embase

signalling.question: 2.2 Were methods additional to database searching used to identify relevant reports?
signalling.quote: backward and forward reference searching of eligible studies was performed using Citationchaser.

signalling.question: 2.3 Were the terms and structure of the search strategy likely to retrieve as many eligible studies as possible?
signalling.quote: A total of 12,774 articles were retrieved, of which 9009 remained after removing duplicates.

signalling.question: 2.4 Were restrictions based on date, publication format, or language appropriate?
signalling.quote: Only articles published in the English language were considered for review.

signalling.question: 2.5 Were efforts made to minimise error in selection of studies?
signalling.quote: Two researchers (R.V., V.A.) independently screened the title and abstracts of the retrieved studies

domains.rationale: Two reviewers independently extracted the data of each included study and two authors appraised each study with PROBAST, the standard tool for prediction-model studies, including its applicability section. Study characteristics, predictors and performance measures were collected into the review's tables.

signalling.question: 3.1 Were efforts made to minimise error in data collection?
signalling.quote: For each included study, two reviewers independently extracted the data (R.V., V.A., J.B.).

signalling.question: 3.2 Were sufficient study characteristics available for both review authors and readers to be able to interpret the results?
signalling.quote: Description of included studies ... Description of the prediction models (Results sections 3.2 and 3.3 with tables).

signalling.question: 3.3 Were all relevant study results collected for use in the synthesis?
signalling.quote: The AUC/Harrell's C ranged from 0.71 to 0.98 in the development studies

signalling.question: 3.4 Was risk of bias (or methodological quality) formally assessed using appropriate criteria?
signalling.quote: The quality of the included studies was evaluated separately by two authors per study

signalling.question: 3.5 Were efforts made to minimise error in risk of bias assessment?
signalling.quote: evaluated separately by two authors per study

domains.rationale: The review is a narrative synthesis with ranges of performance; no meta-analysis was attempted and the reason is not stated, which is defensible given the heterogeneity of predictors and horizons but is not argued. The PROBAST results are reported by domain and are the cited result itself, so they do not depend on a pooling choice. The review states the overall result in two different ways: the Results say most studies were at unclear or high risk, the Discussion says all were at high risk; by PROBAST's rule an overall high rating follows from the analysis domain being high in every study, so the Discussion statement is the consistent one, but the Results wording leaves the count less clear than it should be. Heterogeneity between studies is described rather than analysed.

signalling.question: 4.1 Did the synthesis include all studies that it should?
signalling.quote: After full text screening, 62 articles remained eligible for inclusion in this review.

signalling.question: 4.2 Were all pre-defined analyses reported or departures explained?
signalling.quote: The review does not state whether a meta-analysis was planned; no reason for the narrative synthesis is given (looked for in Methods and Results).

signalling.question: 4.3 Was the synthesis appropriate given the nature and similarity in the research questions, study designs and outcomes across included studies?
signalling.quote: The AUC/Harrell's C ranged from 0.71 to 0.98 in the development studies

signalling.question: 4.4 Was between-study variation (heterogeneity) minimal or addressed in the synthesis?
signalling.quote: models often rely on a wide variety of predictors, some of which are not easily and readily accessible

signalling.question: 4.5 Were the findings robust, e.g. as demonstrated through funnel plot or sensitivity analyses?
signalling.quote: No sensitivity analysis is reported (looked for in Results and Discussion).

signalling.question: 4.6 Were biases in primary studies minimal or addressed in the synthesis?
signalling.quote: The high risk of bias prohibits drawing strong conclusions of the predictive ability and applicability

phase3.question: A. Did the interpretation of findings address all of the concerns identified in Domains 1 to 4?
phase3.quote: A limitation of this systematic review is that we included studies with full-text available in English

phase3.question: B. Was the relevance of identified studies to the review's research question appropriately considered?
phase3.quote: Evaluation focused on included predictors, predictive performance, risk of bias and generalizability.

phase3.question: C. Did the reviewers avoid emphasising results on the basis of their statistical significance?
phase3.quote: there still is no highly valid prediction model available for MCI to dementia conversion risk.

overall: Unclear risk of bias in the review
overall_rationale: The cited result is the review's own PROBAST profile and the conclusion it supports. Domains 1 to 3 are low: the review was registered, searched two databases with citation chasing, screened and appraised in duplicate, and applied the standard tool for prediction-model studies. Domain 4 is unclear: the synthesis is narrative with no stated reason, heterogeneity is described rather than analysed, and the overall PROBAST result is worded two ways (most studies unclear or high in the Results, all high in the Discussion; the PROBAST rule, with the analysis domain high in every study, supports the Discussion wording). The interpretation addresses the English-only restriction and the primary studies' bias but not the synthesis choice, so the overall judgment is unclear rather than low. None of this bears on whether the included models were correctly rated, which is the result the citing sentence uses.

applicability.domain: Relevance to the citing review's question
applicability.rationale: The citing sentence uses the review's appraisal result (all 62 models at high risk of bias, most without external validation) as a statement about the MCI conversion-model literature, which is exactly what the review assessed.
